clue.text: Spicy food for ancient Greeks in battle?

definitions.meaning: highly seasoned Italian sausages, in the plural
the naval battle of 480 BC in which the Greek fleet defeated the Persians

explanation.surface: A question about what ancient Greek soldiers ate on campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Greek rations; the second sense is the sea battle off the island of that name, where the Greeks beat Xerxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the cured, garlicky sausage doubles as the name of the famous Greek naval victory.

clue.text: New York illustrator enters big struggle

indicators.note: to struggle is to writhe about, so these letters thrash into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A New York artist joins a great fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggle' reads as a noun qualified by 'big', but it is the anagram signal. Saul Steinberg drew many covers for The New Yorker.
explanation.definitionFit: Saul Steinberg was the Romanian-born cartoonist famous for his New Yorker drawings, including the 'View of the World from 9th Avenue'.

clue.text: Captions for stories

definitions.meaning: explanatory wording under pictures or on maps

explanation.surface: Labels written for tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the explanatory text beneath an illustration and myths or traditional tales.

clue.text: Novelist who introduced a visitor to the theatre

definitions.text: Novelist who introduced a visitor to the theatre

parts.words: Novelist who introduced a visitor to the theatre
parts.note: the author of The Cruel Sea also wrote a stage play called The Visitor, so he brought 'a visitor' to the theatre

explanation.surface: A writer escorts a guest to a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas Monsarrat, best known for the novel The Cruel Sea, wrote a play titled The Visitor; the clue reads that as showing a guest into the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Monsarrat was the British author of The Cruel Sea who also wrote the play The Visitor.

clue.text: South American ship featured by Feuchtwanger

parts.note: USS, United States Ship, prefixes American naval vessels

explanation.surface: A South American vessel turns up in a German novelist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Lion Feuchtwanger's novel Jew Süss (Jud Süß) is built around the court financier Joseph Süss Oppenheimer; 'South American' wants to be one phrase but splits as S and American ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Süss is the title figure of Lion Feuchtwanger's historical novel, so he is the one the novelist featured.

clue.text: Humorist featured in Arthur Bergson's work

indicators.note: a name featured in a phrase appears within it, so the answer is a run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: A comic writer appears in a philosopher's writings.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'arTHUR BERgson's'. James Thurber was the American humorist and New Yorker cartoonist.
explanation.definitionFit: James Thurber was an American comic writer, author of The Secret Life of Walter Mitty.

clue.text: A clown may, when between a rock and a hard place

definitions.text: A clown may, when between a rock and a hard place

parts.words: A clown may, when between a rock and a hard place
parts.note: Shakespeare's jester in As You Like It bears a name that is also a hard dark stone for testing gold, so the clown is a rock

explanation.surface: A jester in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The jester of As You Like It shares his name with the hard black stone once used to assay gold, so the 'rock and a hard place' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's court fool in As You Like It carries the name of an assaying stone.

clue.text: Poe's teacher?

parts.note: the name of the doomed house in a Poe tale is also an old word for an assistant schoolmaster

explanation.surface: Asking who taught Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe wrote The Fall of the House of Usher; an usher was formerly an under-master in a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher was an assistant schoolmaster, and the word is also the family name in Poe's famous tale.

clue.text: Rubens, creator of Spring Sonata

parts.note: not the Flemish painter but the Welsh novelist of the same surname who wrote Spring Sonata

explanation.surface: The painter Rubens apparently composed a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubens looks like the painter and Spring Sonata like music, but it is a 1979 novel by Bernice Rubens, Booker winner for The Elected Member.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernice Rubens was the Welsh novelist whose books include Spring Sonata.

clue.text: Got up like Thompson's lark

definitions.meaning: stood or came up, past participle
Flora Thompson's book Lark Rise suggests a lark that has gone up

explanation.surface: Someone got out of bed like a bird in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora Thompson wrote Lark Rise to Candleford about rural Oxfordshire; a lark in 'Lark Rise' has ascended.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascended or stood up, as a lark does when it soars.

clue.text: The Spanish spirit of connoisseur of Greek art

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
gin is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A Spanish drink belongs to an expert in Greek sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon sculptures to Britain, now the 'Elgin Marbles'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh Earl of Elgin collected the Parthenon marbles, making him a famous admirer of classical sculpture.

clue.text: Trumpets erroneously sounded by Chatterton and Browning

definitions.text: Trumpets erroneously sounded by Chatterton and Browning

parts.words: Trumpets erroneously sounded by Chatterton and Browning
parts.note: a mistaken form of 'slogan' (a war cry) that these poets took for a horn and used as such

explanation.surface: Two poets blew trumpets badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The word began as a corruption of 'slogan'; Chatterton and Browning ('Dauntless the slug-horn to my lips I set') used it for a trumpet, so it is erroneous.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudo-archaic word for war horns, invented by misreading an old term for a battle cry.

clue.text: Bishop included among scholarly bookmen in Ian Hay's novel…

indicators.note: a name included among other words is contained within them, so read straight through these words

explanation.surface: A bishop appears among the learned characters of an Ian Hay novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'bookmeN IN IAN'. St Ninian was a 5th-century bishop who evangelised southern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Ninian was an early Christian bishop in Scotland.

clue.text: … and Egyptian attendant to enchant him

parts.note: to charm is to enchant
the man named in the previous clue, Ian, carried over by the ellipsis

explanation.surface: Continuing the story, an Egyptian servant tries to bewitch a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue, so 'him' is the Ian mentioned there. Charmian attends Cleopatra in Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmian is one of Cleopatra's waiting-women in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Where Brahms got six curtains?

parts.note: not the composer but Caryl Brahms, co-author with S. J. Simon of the comic novel Six Curtains for a ballerina

explanation.surface: Asks where the composer Brahms took six curtain calls.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms looks like the composer, but Caryl Brahms and S. J. Simon wrote Six Curtains for Stroganova (1945), so the curtains went to her.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional ballerina is the one who receives the six curtains in the title of Brahms and Simon's novel.

clue.text: English-born Belgian artist may also be Norse

indicators.note: a word that may also be another is rearranged into it, so these letters can be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A Belgian painter of English descent might equally be called Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: James Ensor, the Ostend painter of masks and crowds, had an English father.
explanation.definitionFit: James Ensor was a Belgian expressionist painter of English parentage.

clue.text: Intimate opera festival 1,

definitions.meaning: a private conversation between two people, used as an adjective meaning cosy and private
the name of a London festival of new opera

explanation.surface: A small-scale opera festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase for a two-person meeting is also the name of a London festival of new chamber opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means 'head to head', describing a private one-to-one meeting.

clue.text: Among men a strangely great leader

indicators.note: something arranged strangely is out of its usual order, so these words are to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: An odd figure stands out as a leader among men.
explanation.walkthrough: Agamemnon led the Greek host against Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was king of Mycenae and commander of the Greek army in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Union chaps have a date with Furies

parts.note: EU is the European Union
men are chaps
the Ides are a date in the Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month

explanation.surface: Trade-union men have an appointment with angry women.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eumenides ('kindly ones') is the euphemistic Greek name for the Furies and the title of Aeschylus's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'Kindly Ones' is a placatory Greek name given to the avenging goddesses.

clue.text: Deserted location of discreet writers?

parts.note: an abandoned settlement, read as the home of those who write books for others without credit

explanation.surface: Asks where unseen authors live.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghostwriters stay out of sight, so a town full of them would be the abandoned kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement with no remaining inhabitants.

clue.text: Tragically retrospective musician

parts.note: the mythical lyre-player who lost his wife by looking back as they left the underworld

explanation.surface: A musician given to sad nostalgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' is literal: Orpheus looked back at Eurydice and lost her forever.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian singer of myth whose backward glance cost him Eurydice.

clue.text: Rating on warship may be a sort of stoker

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a naval rating
a ram was a warship with a reinforced prow for ramming

explanation.surface: A sailor on a battleship might be a stoker shovelling coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoker' looks like a ship's fireman, but it is the author: Dracula's creator was Bram Stoker, so 'a Bram' is one sort of Stoker.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'a Bram', the name of the Dracula author, is one kind of Stoker.

clue.text: Poet seen as artist by Hunt

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
Leigh Hunt was the Romantic essayist and poet

explanation.surface: A poet regarded as a painter by a critic called Hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' is not a chase but the first name of Leigh Hunt, friend of Keats and Shelley. Sir Walter Raleigh wrote poetry as well as exploring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh, the Elizabethan courtier, was also a noted poet.

clue.text: "On the I thrice presented him a kingly crown" (Julius Caesar)

definitions.text: "On the I thrice presented him a kingly crown" (Julius Caesar)

parts.words: "On the I thrice presented him a kingly crown" (Julius Caesar)
parts.note: the gap in Antony's line about offering Caesar the crown is the name of the Roman feast and its cave

explanation.surface: Mark Antony's line about offering Caesar a crown three times.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has lost the blank between 'the' and 'I'; the missing word names the festival, the Lupercalia, at which Antony offered Caesar the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lupercal was the sacred cave and festival in Rome where Antony offered Caesar the crown.

clue.text: 'It was some poor Abb in one of the upper ——' (Sterne, A Sentimental Journey in France and Italy)

definitions.text: 'It was some poor Abb in one of the upper ——' (Sterne, A Sentimental Journey in France and Italy)

parts.words: 'It was some poor Abb in one of the upper ——' (Sterne, A Sentimental Journey in France and Italy)
parts.note: the missing word is the French term for theatre boxes, used by Sterne of a Paris playhouse

explanation.surface: A quotation from Sterne about a poor abbé in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterne's poor abbé sits up in the theatre boxes; the French word for boxes fills the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Loges are boxes or private compartments in a theatre.

clue.text: Wild evenings in Paris for Italian conductor

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: soirs is French for evenings

explanation.surface: Riotous nights in Paris suit an Italian maestro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles SOIRS, the French for evenings. Mario Rossi was a leading Italian conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario Rossi was a 20th-century Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Predatory magus

definitions.meaning: a small falcon, a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A wizard with predatory instincts.
explanation.walkthrough: The small falcon and Arthur's wizard share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the small falcon and King Arthur's wizard bear this name.

clue.text: Austrian mountain composer

definitions.meaning: the German word for mountain, the language of Austria

explanation.surface: A composer from the Austrian Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: German for mountain, and the surname of Alban, composer of Wozzeck and Lulu.

clue.text: Jungle baby from colourless Staffs town

parts.note: grey is dull and colourless
Stoke-on-Trent is a town in Staffordshire (Staffs)

explanation.surface: A child from the wild comes from a drab Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffs is short for Staffordshire, an English Midlands county. Tarzan was the infant heir of Lord Greystoke, raised by apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, raised as an infant in the African forest, was by birth Lord Greystoke.

clue.text: Nymph could be Diana

indicators.note: what the letters could be is a reshuffling of them into another word

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana is mistaken for a nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water spirit of Greek myth.

clue.text: Verse briefly estimated in a sin, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so EST sits inside the reworked letters
a sin, perhaps, signals that those letters may be in a different order

parts.note: est. is the short form of estimated

explanation.surface: Short estimated verse sounds sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A SIN to SINA, and 'in' puts EST inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is an intricate poetic form of six six-line stanzas.

clue.text: I am the punishment of God", he claimed

definitions.text: I am the punishment of God", he claimed

parts.words: I am the punishment of God", he claimed
parts.note: a boast attributed to the Mongol conqueror after taking Bukhara

explanation.surface: A conqueror's boast that he is divine retribution.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is attributed to the Mongol ruler addressing the people of Bukhara; the clue's opening quote mark is lost in print.
explanation.definitionFit: The words are traditionally credited to Genghis Khan, founder of the Mongol Empire.
